slides.title: Same Word, Different Strategy
bullets: Multichannel and omnichannel are often used as synonyms
The distinction has real consequences for planning and execution
Confusing the two leads to activity without integration

slides.title: One Message, Many Channels
bullets: The same or similar message pushed across visits, email, congresses, networks
Channels are not coordinated beyond sharing a core message
Goal is maximizing reach and frequency of exposure
Channels don't know what happened on the others

slides.title: One Journey, Built From Data
bullets: Channels integrate around a coherent, personalized HCP journey
Prior interactions decide the next content, format and sequence
A field visit can build on what the HCP already read online
Redundancy drops, relevance of each contact rises

slides.title: Activity Metrics vs Journey Metrics
bullets: Multichannel leans on per-channel activity: opens, visits, attendance
Those metrics are evaluated largely in isolation
Omnichannel needs metrics for the cumulative journey
Journey metrics are harder to build, requiring integrated data

slides.title: Most Organizations Are Still in Between
bullets: Multiple channels are already deployed almost everywhere
True data integration around the HCP remains a work in progress
The literature treats it as a goal, not an achieved state

slides.title: Spot Coordination, Don't Just Add a Channel
bullets: Understanding the difference reveals coordination opportunities in your territory
Look for ways to connect with other channels reaching the same HCPs
Avoid operating as one more isolated channel

takeaway.title: Multichannel maximizes reach; omnichannel coordinates a single coherent HCP journey
bullets: Multichannel repeats a message; omnichannel adapts it to prior interactions
Journey-level metrics are harder but are what omnichannel requires
Most organizations still have channels without full integration
